cards.term: "Bless thee, Bottom! bless thee! thou art translated."
cards.def: Peter Quince says this in 3.1.60 when Bottom re-enters with an ass's head, using "translated" to mean changed or transformed.

cards.term: "What angel wakes me from my flowery bed?"
cards.def: Titania, still under Oberon's love-juice, says this in 3.1.65 as she wakes to Bottom's singing.

cards.term: "reason and love keep little company together now-a-days"
cards.def: Bottom says this in 3.1.70 after Titania swears she loves him, joking that reason and love are now strangers.

cards.term: "My mistress with a monster is in love."
cards.def: Puck reports this to Oberon in 3.2.10 after leaving Bottom "translated" for Titania to see when she wakes.

cards.term: "This is the woman; but not this the man."
cards.def: Puck says this in 3.2.45 when Demetrius and Hermia enter, showing Oberon that Puck anointed the wrong Athenian.
Puck says this in 3.2.120 as he and Oberon stand aside to watch Lysander plead with Helena.
Demetrius says this in 3.2.144 when he wakes after Oberon has charmed his eyes, instantly doting on Helena.

cards.term: "And though she be but little, she is fierce."
cards.def: Helena says this of Hermia in 3.2.343, after calling her a vixen at school, which Hermia hears as another insult about her height.

cards.term: "Jack shall have Jill; / Nought shall go ill."
cards.def: Puck recites this country proverb in 3.2.490-494 as he squeezes the remedy onto Lysander's eyes so each man will wake to his own love.

cards.term: "Dian's bud o'er Cupid's flower / Hath such force and blessed power."
cards.def: Oberon says this in 4.1.55-58 as he touches Titania's eyes with an herb to undo the love-juice and release her from Bottom.

cards.term: "Methought I was enamour'd of an ass."
cards.def: Titania says this in 4.1.60 when she wakes, then loathes Bottom's visage once the spell is lifted.
Theseus says this in 4.1.165 after Demetrius declares his love for Helena, ruling that the three couples shall be married in the temple.

cards.term: "it shall be called 'Bottom's Dream,' because it hath no bottom"
cards.def: Bottom, waking in 4.1, plans this ballad of a vision "past the wit of man to say," mixing the senses as he tries to report it.

cards.term: "You must say, 'paragon:' a paramour is, God bless us! a thing of naught."
cards.def: Flute corrects Quince in 4.2 after Quince praises Bottom's voice with the wrong word, "paramour."
